items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 161:1
items.html: (To the question) The aspect of the second Ibur of the externality is the aspect of nine months, because in the first Ibur of the externality, the Ibur of ZA was in the place of the HGT of AA, and he was included only in the VAK of AA; but now, in the second Ibur of the externality, when he is included at the time of his Ibur in the GAR of AA, three months from the GAR of AA are added here, and there are nine months. But in the third Ibur of the internality, there is no novelty in the aspect of the GAR of Atik in which he is included at the time of his Ibur, because also in the second Ibur, at the time he was included in the GAR of AA, he was also included in the GAR of Atik, since by the force of the bowing of the head, the two heads of Atik and AA are considered as one. And all the novelty here is in his inclusion in the ZAT of Atik itself, for since the Ibur was made in the place of the GAR of Atik, it is found that when he is born, he clothes the ZAT of Atik, being the aspect of the upper-lower from the Peh of Atik. Hence it is called the Ibur of seven months, after the ZAT of Atik. (Item 194).
